title: The Job Interview
summary: A first interview — present perfect for experience, going to for plans.
text:
Daniel arrived twenty minutes early. He sat in the waiting room and read his notes again. He had never had a real job interview before, and his hands were cold.

At ten o'clock a woman opened the door. "Daniel? I'm Marta, the manager. Come in."

They sat down and Marta looked at his CV. "You've studied design for three years," she said. "Have you ever worked with clients?"

"Not in a company," Daniel answered honestly. "But I've made websites for two small shops in my neighbourhood, and I've learned a lot from that. I had to explain my ideas to people who don't know anything about design."

Marta wrote something down. "That's useful. Most of our clients aren't designers either." Then she asked, "What are you going to do if a client doesn't like your work?"

Daniel thought for a moment. "I'm going to ask questions until I understand what they really need. Usually the problem isn't the colour or the font. It's that we haven't agreed on the goal."

Marta smiled for the first time. "Good answer. We'll call you on Friday."

They called on Thursday.

questions.q: How did Daniel feel before the interview?
What experience does Daniel have with clients?
Why does Marta find his experience useful?
What does Daniel say the real problem usually is?
When did the company call him?
